notes: Raw schematic and supplied component overlays/crops were used as visual aids only; no OCR engines, Ground Truth, GT-derived feedback, Raw+wires folders, or web resources were used.
All Diego asserted edges were visually checked and retained; no asserted edge was removed because each retained edge has a visible solid conductor or direct dashed interlock termination.
Node IDs from Diego were preserved; only component type classifications were refined for source, generator, transfer switch, relay, charger, inverter, and ESF logic nodes.
Filled dots at bus taps were treated as electrical connections; visual crossings without filled dots were not used for connectivity.
Bottom ESF/RPS dashed cable-tray or distribution routing was not converted into point-to-point matrix connectivity unless a solid feed or direct dashed termination was visible.
Diego round 2 adopts Jennifer round 1 exactly for node IDs/order, asserted edge set, uncertain edge set, rejected non-edges, and matrix connectivity.

diego_round2_review.summary: Re-inspection of the raw schematic and allowed crops supports Jennifer's precision refinements: asserted edges remain unchanged, only three uncertain candidates remain, and the bottom dashed ESF/RPS tray candidates are rejected because they do not visibly terminate point-to-point.
visual_basis: P07/P08 terminate at CB-TIE-6K and the bus taps on BUS-6KA/BUS-6KB are visible, but a direct GRID-345-to-CB-TIE-6K termination is not visually clear.
C01 and C04 visibly terminate between ATS-1A/RELAY-K12A and RELAY-K12B/ATS-1B respectively; C02/C05 near PLC-ESF lack clear point-to-point relay termination.
Bottom C03/C06 and tray routing are functional dashed routing annotations rather than discrete visible terminations among PAN-RPS, INST-RACK, and PLC-ESF nodes.
